title: Command: supersede
lead:
`adj supersede OLD --by NEW` links two decided records and marks OLD as
`superseded`.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** lint for supersede cycles.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Goal 4: supersede a decision while keeping its history.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/commands/supersede.go`.
- `internal/model/transition.go`: the decided -> superseded transition from S03
  (extend only if needed).
- `internal/cli/supersede_test.go`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
End-to-end CLI tests call `cli.Run` in a fresh `t.TempDir()` store (with
`t.Chdir`, which rules out `t.Parallel`, or a root option the implementer adds
and records under C32), with a fixed clock where dates matter.

- After `supersede A --by B`: A is `superseded`, A.superseded_by is B,
  B.supersedes includes A, and each gets one history entry.
- `context` no longer lists A; `show A` still prints A and its history
  (acceptance criterion).
- A not decided, B not decided, A equal to B, or an unknown ID exits non-zero
  and leaves both records unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Load both records, apply both changes in memory and validate them, then write
both through `store.Update`. Nothing is written unless both records pass.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run from the repo root after `. scripts/env.sh` (the in-repo cache env, C33;
use the equivalent AGENTS.md names if S02 chose another):

- `go test ./...` passes, including this slice's new tests.
- `go vet ./...` reports nothing.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing (not `gofmt -l .`, which also walks
  `.cache/` and `.worktrees/`).
- Each interface choice made in this slice is a slicer catalog decision with a
  one-line reason (C32).
- `slicer check --json` is clean.
